note: Known-item queries; relevance is any chunk of the target file. Each was written by reading the target and describing it the way someone who remembers the document but not its words would.

queries.query: Which benchmark tooling tells me whether a cheap model is good enough to run the analytical operators, by running the same input twice and then scoring against a deliberately broken copy?
What's the guidance on naming a collection when I save notes - can I name it after the project I'm working on this month?
How do I get an agent inside a dev container to use the storage service running on my laptop instead of starting its own?
If I already have a local setup with a lot of notes, can I carry them over to the hosted service, or do I start from scratch?
Which editors and command-line tools other than Claude can launch the nexus tool server, and what does the setup look like for one of them?
If an older engine release has to take over a machine that a newer one already migrated, what should I do with the existing database directory before it boots?
When a reusable retrieval recipe needs values from the caller, who wins if the template and the caller both supply the same one, and what happens when a mandatory one is missing?
A local install is supposed to keep everything on my machine. Under what configuration does it start sending my text to an outside embedding provider, and does a restart switch that off?
Which of the retrieval entry points favours chunks that are linked to design records, and which one ignores the link graph?
Why couldn't I remove a single entry from the memory store without hand-editing the database file, and which storage layers got a delete verb as the fix?
After the embedding-model mismatch slipped through several release candidates, what follow-up closed the testing and tooling holes, and which collection tools were added for agents?
How was a reviewing agent supposed to learn what the implementer had already tried and found fragile earlier in the same session?
Why do agents call work finished when pieces are unwired, and what two-layer hook design was proposed to catch that before a task gets closed?
Why did slash commands break when their startup script printed markdown fences, and what was chosen instead of inlining shell in the command file?
Two stores claimed to know which collections belong to a repository and they disagreed; which design record proposes dropping the per-user JSON registry in favour of the catalog?
A migration was refused by the service for a 384-dimension model; what had gone stale in the classifier that mirrors the service's embedders?
How was nexus supposed to index content that lives in somebody's Obsidian vault without copying the text itself into its own tables?
A record that gets read fifty times just lives longer in the short-term store; which proposal turns access counts into actually moving things between memory tiers?
Which of the three memory layers evaporates when the session ends and which one is permanent, and how do I merge two near-duplicate notes?
Where do the checked-in multi-agent scripts live for reviewing with majority-vote verification and for tracing unused wiring, and what is each one for?
How does the indexer cut a source file into pieces - does it understand the language's structure, and what does it do with a file it cannot parse?
What decides that a vector collection is leftover test debris, one that has chunks in it but no live catalog documents pointing at it?
Where is the tiny map of knowledge topics generated and cached so a session can inject it almost instantly at start?
On Windows, what retries a file rename while an antivirus scan holds the file, and how do we move a group of files so a failure leaves nothing half installed?
Which module picks the offline embedding model for a zero-configuration setup, preferring the bigger 768-dimension one when its library is installed?
Where is the small ranking-model file that the Java engine's local reranker needs downloaded and checksum-verified?
Is there a checker that reads markdown and warns when a documented collection name or a quoted chunk count has drifted out of date?
What leaves a local trail showing the trash purge ran, so doctor can tell an empty audit table from a purge that never happened?
Where do we log, once per distinct shape, which metadata keys a client sends with tool calls, without ever recording the values?
What fixes the hang where the first numpy import inside a tool call freezes the Windows server because a read is stuck on its input pipe?
Why isn't the session lease good enough as a signal that the tool server is ready to talk, and what file stands in for it?
Which file records that an install is in the middle of an upgrade so other long-running processes show a warning banner and pause their work?
How are plan templates gathered from the built-in directory, accepted design records and the project folder before they are stored?
Where are the counts of how often each routing hook rule fired, allowed, blocked or was escaped computed for the thirty-day review?
How does a message addressed to a name get turned into a concrete mailbox, and what tells a session identifier from an agent identifier?
What builds the instruction a session receives at startup telling it to subscribe to its own mailbox, and checks that the tuple surface exists first?
What warns us out loud when two different owners end up with separate catalog entries for the same file path?
Which helper turns a comma-separated key=value string with comparison operators into a metadata filter shared by the command line and the tools?
Where is the command group for issuing, rotating and revoking bridge tokens, and why can the token only be displayed once?
Which thin client talks to the Java aspects service to store and look up highlights, mirroring the interface of the old local store?
